title: Extension to the Study of Efficacy of CDZ173 in Patients With APDS/PASLI
off: An Open-label, Non-randomized Extension Study to Evaluate the Long Term Safety, Tolerability, Efficacy and Pharmacokinetics of CDZ173 in Patients With APDS/PASLI (Activated Phosphoinositide 3-kinase Delta Syndrome/p110δ-activating Mutation Causing Senescent T Cells, Lymphadenopathy and Immunodeficiency)
summary: This study is designed to provide long-term CDZ173 treatment, a selective PI3Kδ inhibitor, to the patients with genetically activated PI3Kδ, i.e., patients with APDS/PASLI who participated in the CCDZ173X2201 study or who were treated previously with PI3Kδ inhibitors other than CDZ173. The study is open-label designed to establish the long-term safety, tolerability, efficay and pharmacokinetics of CDZ173 in the target population.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Written informed consent must be obtained before any assessment is performed.
* Paients must have participated in the study CCDZ173X2201 or were treated previously with PI3Kδ inhibitors other than CDZ173.
* Patients who are deemed by the Investigator to benefit from PI3Kδ inhibitor therapy.
* Patients or their legal representatives (for patients under the age of 18 years) must be able to communicate well with the Investigator, to understand and comply with the requirements of the study.
* Documented APDS/PASLI-associated genetic PI3K delta mutation.

Exclusion Criteria:

\- Any medically significant disease or condition that is unrelated to APDS/PASLI

Other protocol-defined inclusion/exclusion criteria may apply.

abstracts:
Rao VK, Šedivá A, Dalm VASH, Plebani A, Schuetz C, Shcherbina A, et al. Open-label extension study of leniolisib in activated PI3Kδ syndrome: Long-term efficacy and safety. J Hum Immun. 2026. doi: 10.70962/jhi.20260040
Activated phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta syndrome (APDS) is an inborn error of immunity characterized by immune deficiency and dysregulation. Leniolisib is a selective phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta inhibitor approved to treat APDS in patients ≥12 years old. We report final results from a single-arm, open-label extension study in 37 patients with APDS (NCT02859727). Median leniolisib exposure was 4.3 years (range, 1.2-7.0 years). Adverse events (AE) were reported in 34 patients; 87% were grade 1. Serious AEs, reported in 10 patients, were deemed unrelated to leniolisib. Two patients discontinued treatment due to AEs: cardiac arrest and Hodgkin's lymphoma. There were significant reductions in annual infection (P = 0.0005) and respiratory infection (P = 0.0017) rates per year of treatment. Immunoglobulin replacement therapy (IRT) use significantly decreased per year of treatment (P = 0.0095). Clinically meaningful improvements in general health scores from the 36-Item Short Form Survey were observed. Overall, long-term use of leniolisib was generally well tolerated, and infections and IRT use reduced over time.

Rao VK, Morgan A, Torgerson TR, Harrington A, Whalen J, Munro E, et al. Evaluating the impact of leniolisib treatment on symptoms and health-related quality of life in activated phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta (PI3Kδ) syndrome. Front Immunol. 2026. doi: 10.3389/fimmu.2026.1739437
PURPOSE: Activated phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta (PI3Kδ) syndrome (APDS) is an ultra-rare inborn error of immunity, characterised by immune deficiency and dysregulation. In a randomised controlled trial (RCT; NCT02435173) and open-label extension (OLE; NCT02859727), leniolisib, a selective PI3Kδ inhibitor, was efficacious and well-tolerated in individuals with APDS. These trials suggested some improvements with leniolisib in health-related quality of life (HRQoL) using generic instruments, with other anecdotal evidence also describing improvements in specific domains. Here, all available qualitative data relating to treatment experience were systematically assessed to evaluate any perceived impacts of leniolisib on patients' lives.
METHODS: Changes in APDS-related symptoms and patient HRQoL were assessed using unsolicited qualitative data captured from 36 leniolisib-treated individuals: RCT and OLE clinician-recorded, open-text patient narratives (n=31); case reports (n=4); standalone qualitative study conducted with APDS patient/caregiver interviews/narratives (n=1).
RESULTS: Improvements in APDS-related symptoms and HRQoL were reported following treatment with leniolisib: 86.1% (31/36) of individuals mentioned improvements in ≥1 symptom/HRQoL impact. Of these, 87.1% (27/31) explicitly attributed ≥1 improvement to leniolisib. One-third (12/36) of individuals explicitly attributed improvements in fatigue/energy to leniolisib. This was associated with reported HRQoL improvements explicitly attributed to leniolisib: physical activity (33.3% [12/36]), work/school performance/attendance (13.9% [5/36]) and travel ability (8.3% [3/36]). Moreover, 36.1% (13/36) of participants explicitly attributed improvements in their overall wellbeing to leniolisib.
CONCLUSION: As data were unsolicited and baseline symptoms/HRQoL were not available, results may not represent all changes experienced, and is not possible to determine the amount of change in symptoms/HRQoL associated with leniolisib. Nevertheless, these analyses indicate that participants with APDS experienced improvements in symptoms and overall wellbeing following treatment with leniolisib.

Whalen J, Chandra A, Kracker S, Ehl S, Seidel MG, Gulas I, et al. Comparative efficacy of leniolisib (CDZ173) versus standard of care on rates of respiratory tract infection and serum immunoglobulin M (IgM) levels among individuals with activated phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta (PI3Kδ) syndrome (APDS): an externally controlled study. Clin Exp Immunol. 2025. doi: 10.1093/cei/uxae107
Leniolisib, an oral, targeted phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta (PI3Kδ) inhibitor, was well-tolerated and efficacious versus placebo in treating individuals with activated PI3Kδ syndrome (APDS), an ultra-rare inborn error of immunity (IEI), in a 12-week randomised controlled trial. However, longer-term comparative data versus standard of care are lacking. This externally controlled study compared the long-term effects of leniolisib on annual rate of respiratory tract infections and change in serum immunoglobulin M (IgM) levels versus current standard of care, using data from the leniolisib single-arm open-label extension study 2201E1 (NCT02859727) and the European Society for Immunodeficiencies (ESID) registry. The endpoints were chosen following feasibility assessment considering comparability and availability of data from both sources. Baseline characteristics between groups were balanced through inverse probability of treatment weighting. The leniolisib-treated group included 37 participants, with 62 and 49 participants in the control group for the respiratory tract infections and serum IgM analyses, respectively. Significant reductions in the annual rate of respiratory tract infections (rate ratio: 0.34; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.19, 0.59) and serum IgM levels (treatment effect: -1.09 g/L; 95% CI: -1.78, -0.39, P = 0.002) were observed in leniolisib-treated individuals versus standard of care. The results were consistent across all sensitivity analyses, regardless of censoring, baseline infection rate definition, missing data handling, or covariate selection. x.titre: Extension à long terme du léniolisib (CDZ173) dans le syndrome APDS/PASLI
x.question: Le léniolisib reste-t-il sûr et efficace au long cours chez les patients atteints de syndrome APDS/PASLI ?
x.contexte:
Le syndrome APDS (PASLI) est un déficit immunitaire primitif rare lié à des mutations activatrices de la sous-unité p110δ de la PI3K (gènes PIK3CD ou PIK3R1). Il associe infections récidivantes, lymphoprolifération (adénopathies, splénomégalie), cytopénies auto-immunes et risque accru de lymphome. Les traitements classiques sont symptomatiques : substitution en immunoglobulines, antibioprophylaxie, immunosuppresseurs comme le sirolimus, parfois greffe de cellules souches.

Le léniolisib (CDZ173) est un inhibiteur sélectif oral de PI3Kδ, qui corrige la voie hyperactivée. Il a été évalué dans l'étude de phase 2 CCDZ173X2201 puis dans un essai randomisé de phase 3. Cette étude d'extension ouverte, sans comparateur, propose le traitement prolongé aux patients de ces essais ou déjà traités par d'autres inhibiteurs de PI3Kδ. Elle avait pour but de suivre la tolérance, l'efficacité et la pharmacocinétique à long terme. L'étude est terminée avant son terme prévu ; 37 patients âgés de 12 à 75 ans ont reçu 140 mg par jour.
x.interet: Ce suivi de plus de six ans documente la tolérance à long terme d'un inhibiteur de PI3Kδ ciblé, utile pour juger de l'intérêt d'un traitement chronique dans une maladie ultra-rare.
x.profil: Des patients de 12 à 75 ans atteints de syndrome APDS/PASLI avec mutation PI3Kδ documentée.
inclusion: Participation à l'étude CCDZ173X2201 ou traitement antérieur par un autre inhibiteur de PI3Kδ
Mutation génétique activatrice de PI3Kδ documentée (APDS/PASLI)
Bénéfice attendu d'un inhibiteur de PI3Kδ selon l'investigateur
Capacité à communiquer et à respecter le protocole
exclusion: Maladie ou état médical significatif sans rapport avec l'APDS/PASLI
Autres critères du protocole : non précisé
x.critere: Nombre de participants avec événements indésirables (graves ou non) sous léniolisib, sur 6 ans et 3 mois
x.resultats: L'étude a inclus 37 participants, tous traités par léniolisib (CDZ173). Le critère principal est un critère de tolérance, sans comparaison. Les 37 participants (100 %) ont présenté au moins un événement indésirable, grave ou non. Dix participants ont présenté au moins un événement indésirable grave et un décès est rapporté. Le registre ne détaille pas d'analyse d'efficacité ni de conclusion des investigateurs. L'étude a été arrêtée avant son terme.
